readmeExcerpt:
Development at the speed of light.

         

   

     

           


## What is SpacetimeDB? SpacetimeDB is a relational database that is also a server. You upload your application logic directly into the database, and clients connect to it without any server in between. It is built for reactive applications, where every client sees changes as they happen: web apps like collaborative tools, dashboards, and chat, as well as multiplayer games. Write your schema and business logic as a **module** in [Rust](https://spacetimedb.com/docs/quickstarts/rust), [C#](https://spacetimedb.com/docs/quickstarts/c-sharp), [TypeScript](https://spacetimedb.com/docs/quickstarts/typescript), or [C++](https://spacetimedb.com/docs/quickstarts/c-plus-plus). SpacetimeDB compiles it, runs it inside the database, and automatically synchronizes state to connected clients in real-time. Instead of deploying a web or game server that sits in between your clients and your database, your clients connect directly to the database and execute your application logic in your module. You can write all of your permission and authorization logic right inside your module just as you would in a normal server. This means that you can write your entire application in a single language and deploy it as a single binary. No more separate webserver, no more containers, no more Kubernetes, no more VMs, no more DevOps, no more caching later. Zero infrastructure to manage. SpacetimeDB is optimized for maximum speed and minimum latency. SpacetimeDB provides all the ACID guarantees of a traditional RDBMS, with all the speed of an optimized web server. Hot data stays in memory for fast access and colder data lives on disk, while a commit log provides [durability](#durability) and crash recovery. The entire backend of our MMORPG [BitCraft Online](https://bitcraftonline.com) runs as a single SpacetimeDB module: chat, items, terrain, player positions, everything, synchronized to thousands of players in real-time. ## Quick Start ### 1. Install ```bash # macOS / Linux curl -sSf https://install.spacetimedb.com | sh # Windows (PowerShell) iwr https://windows.spacetimedb.com -useb | iex ``` ### 2. Log in ```bash spacetime login ``` This opens a browser to authenticate with GitHub. Your identity is linked to your account so you can publish databases. ### 3. Start developing ```bash spacetime dev --template chat-react-ts ``` That is it. This creates a project from a template, publishes it to [Maincloud](https://spacetimedb.com/docs/how-to/deploy/maincloud), and watches for file changes, automatically rebuilding and republishing on save. See [pricing](https://spacetimedb.com/pricing) for details. ## How It Works SpacetimeDB modules define **tables** (your data) and **reducers** (your logic). Clients connect, call reducers, and subscribe to tables. When data changes, SpacetimeDB pushes updates to subscribed clients automatically. ```rust // Define a table #[spacetimedb::table(accessor = messages, public)] pub struct Message { #[primary_key] #[auto_inc] id: u64, sender: Identity, text: String, } // Define a reducer (your API endpoint) #[spacetimedb::reducer] pub fn send_message(ctx: &ReducerContext, text: String) { ctx.db.messages().insert(Message { id: 0, sender: ctx.sender, text, }); } ``` On the client side, subscribe and get live updates: ```typescript const [messages] = useTable(tables.message); // messages updates automatically when the server state changes. // No polling. No refetching. ``` ## Use Cases SpacetimeDB is well suited to web application backends, from everyday CRUD apps to reactive ones like collaborative tools, live dashboards, and chat. Write your module in TypeScript and connect from the browser with the [TypeScript SDK](https://spacetimedb.com/docs/clients/typescript), which includes React hooks like `useTable` and integrations for Vue, Svelte, Angular, and other frameworks. Each reducer runs as an ACID transaction, and subscribed clients receive committed changes automatically, so you don't need polling, a separate API server, or a pub/sub layer to keep them in sync. The `chat-react-ts` template from the Quick Start is a working example. SpacetimeDB is optimized for low-latency transactional workloads like these, rather than batch processing or analytical queries. ## Durability Every transaction that changes data is written to an on-disk [commitlog](https://spacetimedb.com/docs/reference/internals/commitlog), which is replayed to recover the database after a crash. Transactions are fsynced in batches, so many transactions share a single `fsync` (group commit) ([`local.rs`](crates/durability/src/imp/local.rs)). Since SpacetimeDB 2.0, clients get [confirmed reads](https://spacetimedb.com/docs/upgrade#confirmed-reads-enabled-by-default) by default: the server holds back a transaction's subscription updates, and the caller's reducer result, until that transaction is durable ([`client_connection.rs`](crates/core/src/client/client_connection.rs)), so the data a client receives from its subscriptions and reducer calls will survive a crash. SQL queries over HTTP wait for durability by default too. On Maincloud and other replicated deployments, durable instead means [persisted by the replicas the database's replication settings require](https://spacetimedb.com/docs/clients/typescript#method-withconfirmedreads). Apps that can tolerate a client occasionally seeing a write that is then lost in a crash, like many games, can opt out with `withConfirmedReads(false)` for lower latency. ## Language Support ### Server Modules Write your database logic in any of these languages: | Language | Quickstart | |----------|-----------| | **Rust** | [Get started](https://spacetimedb.com/docs/quickstarts/rust) | | **C#** | [Get started](https://spacetimedb.com/docs/quickstarts/c-sharp) | | **TypeScript** | [Get started](https://spacetimedb.com/docs/quickstarts/typescript) | | **C++** | [Get started](https://spacetimedb.com/docs/quickstarts/c-plus-plus) | ### Client SDKs Connect from any of these platforms: | SDK | Quickstart | |-----|-----------| | **TypeScript** (React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte, Angular, Node.js, Bun, Deno) | [Get started](https://spacetimedb.com/docs/quickstarts/react) | | **Rust** | [Get started](https://spacetimedb.com/docs/quickstarts/rust) | | **C#** (standalone and Unity) | [Get started](https://spacetimedb.com/docs/quickstarts/c-sharp) | | **C++** (Unreal Engine) | [Get started](https://spacetimedb.com/docs/quickstarts/c-plus-plus) | ## Running with Docker ```bash docker run --rm --pull always -p 3000:3000 clockworklabs/spacetime start ``` ## Building from Source If you need features from `master` that have not been released yet: ```bash # Prerequisites: Rust toolchain with wasm32-unknown-unknown target curl https://sh.rustup.rs -sSf | sh git clone https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB cd SpacetimeDB cargo build --locked --release -p spacetimedb-standalone -p spacetimedb-update -p spacetimedb-cli ``` Then install the binaries:

readmeHtml:
Development at the speed of light.

         

   

     

           


What is SpacetimeDB?

SpacetimeDB is a relational database that is also a server. You upload your application logic directly into the database, and clients connect to it without any server in between. It is built for reactive applications, where every client sees changes as they happen: web apps like collaborative tools, dashboards, and chat, as well as multiplayer games.

Write your schema and business logic as a module in Rust, C#, TypeScript, or C++. SpacetimeDB compiles it, runs it inside the database, and automatically synchronizes state to connected clients in real-time.

Instead of deploying a web or game server that sits in between your clients and your database, your clients connect directly to the database and execute your application logic in your module. You can write all of your permission and authorization logic right inside your module just as you would in a normal server.

This means that you can write your entire application in a single language and deploy it as a single binary. No more separate webserver, no more containers, no more Kubernetes, no more VMs, no more DevOps, no more caching later. Zero infrastructure to manage.

SpacetimeDB application architecture
(elements in white are provided by SpacetimeDB)

SpacetimeDB is optimized for maximum speed and minimum latency. SpacetimeDB provides all the ACID guarantees of a traditional RDBMS, with all the speed of an optimized web server. Hot data stays in memory for fast access and colder data lives on disk, while a commit log provides durability and crash recovery. The entire backend of our MMORPG BitCraft Online runs as a single SpacetimeDB module: chat, items, terrain, player positions, everything, synchronized to thousands of players in real-time.

Quick Start

1. Install

# macOS / Linux
curl -sSf https://install.spacetimedb.com | sh

# Windows (PowerShell)
iwr https://windows.spacetimedb.com -useb | iex

2. Log in

spacetime login

This opens a browser to authenticate with GitHub. Your identity is linked to your account so you can publish databases.

3. Start developing

spacetime dev --template chat-react-ts

That is it. This creates a project from a template, publishes it to Maincloud, and watches for file changes, automatically rebuilding and republishing on save. See pricing for details.

How It Works

SpacetimeDB modules define tables (your data) and reducers (your logic). Clients connect, call reducers, and subscribe to tables. When data changes, SpacetimeDB pushes updates to subscribed clients automatically.

// Define a table
#[spacetimedb::table(accessor = messages, public)]
pub struct Message {
    #[primary_key]
    #[auto_inc]
    id: u64,
    sender: Identity,
    text: String,
}

// Define a reducer (your API endpoint)
#[spacetimedb::reducer]
pub fn send_message(ctx: &ReducerContext, text: String) {
    ctx.db.messages().insert(Message {
        id: 0,
        sender: ctx.sender,
        text,
    });
}

On the client side, subscribe and get live updates:

const [messages] = useTable(tables.message);
// messages updates automatically when the server state changes.
// No polling. No refetching.

Use Cases

SpacetimeDB is well suited to web application backends, from everyday CRUD apps to reactive ones like collaborative tools, live dashboards, and chat. Write your module in TypeScript and connect from the browser with the TypeScript SDK, which includes React hooks like useTable and integrations for Vue, Svelte, Angular, and other frameworks. Each reducer runs as an ACID transaction, and subscribed clients receive committed changes automatically, so you don't need polling, a separate API server, or a pub/sub layer to keep them in sync. The chat-react-ts template from the Quick Start is a working example.

SpacetimeDB is optimized for low-latency transactional workloads like these, rather than batch processing or analytical queries.

Durability

Every transaction that changes data is written to an on-disk commitlog, which is replayed to recover the database after a crash. Transactions are fsynced in batches, so many transactions share a single fsync (group commit) (local.rs).

Since SpacetimeDB 2.0, clients get confirmed reads by default: the server holds back a transaction's subscription updates, and the caller's reducer result, until that transaction is durable (client_connection.rs), so the data a client receives from its subscriptions and reducer calls will survive a crash. SQL queries over HTTP wait for durability by default too. On Maincloud and other replicated deployments, durable instead means persisted by the replicas the database's replication settings require. Apps that can tolerate a client occasionally seeing a write that is then lost in a crash, like many games, can opt out with withConfirmedReads(false) for lower latency.

Language Support

Server Modules

Write your database logic in any of these languages:

Language Quickstart
Rust Get started
C# Get started
TypeScript Get started
C++ Get started

Client SDKs

Connect from any of these platforms:

SDK Quickstart
TypeScript (React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte, Angular, Node.js, Bun, Deno) Get started
Rust Get started
C# (standalone and Unity) Get started
C++ (Unreal Engine) Get started

Running with Docker

docker run --rm --pull always -p 3000:3000 clockworklabs/spacetime start

Building from Source

If you need features from master that have not been released yet:

# Prerequisites: Rust toolchain with wasm32-unknown-unknown target
curl https://sh.rustup.rs -sSf | sh

git clone https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB
cd SpacetimeDB
cargo build --locked --release -p spacetimedb-standalone -p spacetimedb-update -p spacetimedb-cli

Then install the binaries:

macOS / Linux 
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
STDB_VERSION="$(./target/release/spacetimedb-cli --version | sed -n 's/.*spacetimedb tool version \([0-9.]*\);.*/\1/p')"
mkdir -p ~/.local/share/spacetime/bin/$STDB_VERSION

cp target/release/spacetimedb-update ~/.local/bin/spacetime
cp target/release/spacetimedb-cli ~/.local/share/spacetime/bin/$STDB_VERSION
cp target/release/spacetimedb-standalone ~/.local/share/spacetime/bin/$STDB_VERSION

# Add to your shell config if not already present:
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# Set the active version:
spacetime version use $STDB_VERSION
Windows (PowerShell) 
$stdbDir = "$HOME\AppData\Local\SpacetimeDB"
$stdbVersion = & ".\target\release\spacetimedb-cli" --version |
    Select-String -Pattern 'spacetimedb tool version ([0-9.]+);' |
    ForEach-Object { $_.Matches.Groups[1].Value }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "$stdbDir\bin\$stdbVersion" -Force | Out-Null

Copy-Item "target\release\spacetimedb-update.exe" "$stdbDir\spacetime.exe"
Copy-Item "target\release\spacetimedb-cli.exe" "$stdbDir\bin\$stdbVersion\"
Copy-Item "target\release\spacetimedb-standalone.exe" "$stdbDir\bin\$stdbVersion\"

# Add to your system PATH: %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\SpacetimeDB
# Then in a new shell:
spacetime version use $stdbVersion

Verify with spacetime --version.

To find your way around the code, see the architecture diagram of what runs inside SpacetimeDB Standalone.

Documentation

To set up a coding agent such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor, paste this prompt into it. It points the agent to the agent setup guide.

Set yourself up to build with Spacetime (SpacetimeDB).

1. Read https://spacetimedb.com/agent-setup.md carefully, in full rather than a summary, and follow it. Run the commands yourself, and ask me only for approvals, logins, or restarts.
2. Read https://spacetimedb.com/docs/intro/misconceptions/ carefully, in full. Spacetime has changed a lot, so what you remember about it, and older articles online, may be out of date. When you describe Spacetime or compare it with other backends, go by the current docs.
3. Tell me what you installed, what you verified, and anything I still need to do.

Full documentation is available at spacetimedb.com/docs, including:

  • Quickstart guides for every supported language and framework
  • Core concepts: tables, reducers, subscriptions, authentication
  • Tutorials: chat app, Unity multiplayer, Unreal Engine multiplayer
  • Deployment guide: publishing to Maincloud
  • CLI reference
  • SQL reference

License

SpacetimeDB is licensed under the Business Source License 1.1 (BSL). It converts to the AGPL v3.0 with a linking exception after a few years. The linking exception means you are not required to open-source your own code if you use SpacetimeDB. You only need to contribute back changes to SpacetimeDB itself.

Why did we choose this license? We chose to license SpacetimeDB under the MariaDB Business Source License for 4 years because we can't compete with AWS while also building our products for them.

We chose GPLv3 with linking exception as the open source license because we want contributions merged back into mainline (just like Linux), but we don't want to make anyone else open source their own code (i.e. linking exception).

## Bug Fixes

### Refresh TLS trust following the eMudhra/emSign CA incident

Updated TLS certificate verification dependencies and refreshed certificate trust stores in distributed container images to address the eMudhra/emSign certificate authority key compromise. The updated WebPKI verifier rejects the compromised intermediate keys, and affected roots are removed from the Nix development environment's CA bundle.

Operators should upgrade their SpacetimeDB binaries and container images. See the [RustSec advisory](<https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0382.html>) for details about the upstream incident.

([#6366](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6366>))

### Preserve UUID and branded primitive types in TypeScript

TypeScript type inference now preserves `Uuid` values and branded primitives instead of expanding them into structural records. UUID columns retain their `Uuid` type, and branded strings remain assignable to `string`. This is a types-only fix with no runtime behavior change.

([#5971](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/5971>))

releases.name: Release v2.14.0
releases.body:
## New Features

### 🚀 Async inter-database communication 🚀 

Rust and TypeScript modules can now call reducers in other databases asynchronously through declared dependencies and generated receiver bindings. A module declares its dependencies in `spacetime.json`, referencing either a local module path or a published database, and `spacetime generate` produces typed receiver bindings for each dependency, while `spacetime dev` publishes dependency databases alongside the main one.

Senders enqueue calls by inserting rows into generated outbox tables, which are insert-only and map their columns to the receiver's reducer parameters with compile-time type checking. Delivery is handled by a new IDC actor that manages concurrent outbox streams over HTTP/2, and optional `on_result` / `onResult` callbacks report delivery outcomes back to the sender. Dependencies are namespaced by name, so a module can depend on two databases that export identically named types.

Note: C# and C++ Async IDC are coming in a future release.

releases.name: Release v2.13.0
releases.body:
## New Features

### Reusable TypeScript submodules

TypeScript modules can now use a collection of reusable submodules for common application needs. The initial packages provide cron-style and interval scheduling, retry with exponential backoff, fixed-window rate limiting, cryptographic and encoding helpers, and Resend email integration.

The packages include typed APIs, installation documentation, tests, and examples. They can be installed in projects using SpacetimeDB 2.12 or later.

([#5903](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/5903>), [#6158](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6158>), [#6309](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6309>))

### C# module submodules and namespaces

C# modules can now compose separately built module assemblies as submodules. Assembly-level namespace declarations control how a dependency is exposed in C# and, optionally, its canonical database namespace.

releases.name: Release v2.12.0
releases.body:
## New Features

### Persistent typed database environments

SpacetimeDB modules can now declare typed environment variables for configuration and secrets. Rust, TypeScript, C#, and C++ modules can read declared values through their execution context, with support for required and optional strings as well as constrained sets of allowed values.

Values can come from project configuration or the publishing process's environment. They are validated against the module's declarations and updated atomically with a module publish. Stored values are preserved by default across publishes, while `--env-only`, `--unset-env`, and `--replace-env` support configuration changes without replacing the module. Authorized users can inspect published values with `spacetime env get` and `spacetime env list`.

([#5887](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/5887>), [#5961](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/5961>), [#6004](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6004>))

### Automatic reconnect for TypeScript and C# clients

The TypeScript and C# SDKs can now keep a `DbConnection`, its client cache, subscriptions, table handles, and registered callbacks

releases.name: Release v2.11.0
releases.body:
# SpacetimeDB v2.11.0

## Security Notice

On September 1, we became aware of a security vulnerability in SpacetimeDB that allowed an attacker who knew a token’s subject and issuer to impersonate the corresponding Identity. We released a [patch](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/5866>) on September 4 in v2.10.0, upgrading our JWT authentication library to address the issue. We waited 30 days after the release before publicly disclosing the vulnerability to give users time to upgrade. We recommend that everyone running an earlier version upgrade to v2.10.0 or later as soon as possible to avoid being affected by this vulnerability.

We are not aware of any instances of the vulnerability being actively exploited in the wild.

## New Features

### Human-readable database descriptions

`spacetime describe` can now print a readable description of a database schema in addition to its machine-readable form. The output makes it easier to inspect tables, reducers, types, indexes, constraints, sequences, schedules, and row-level security rules directly from the CLI.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A unified platform merging relational databases and application servers via WebAssembly for ultra-low latency apps.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: SpacetimeDB radically merges the traditional relational database layer directly with the application logic layer, compiling everything seamlessly into WebAssembly. This highly innovative architecture completely eliminates the absolute need for separate, complex backend servers and databases, entirely removing network latency between the app tier and data tier. By running the critical application code directly alongside the stored data in the exact same process space, it consistently delivers incredible microsecond latency. It is particularly targeted at empowering multiplayer games and highly real-time collaboration applications that demand massive speed. Developers simply write their backend logic as highly modular server-side functions that are automatically and instantly exposed to clients with real-time state synchronization.
keyFeatures: Unified Architecture: Completely combines the complex application server and the massive database into a single, highly cohesive execution engine.
WebAssembly Runtime: Rapidly executes user-provided business logic compiled directly to WASM for incredibly high performance, deep portability, and strong security.
Zero Network Overhead: Entirely eliminates the typical, massive latency associated with querying a traditional database from an entirely separate external server.
Real-Time Subscriptions: Actively allows connected clients to easily subscribe to complex database queries and rapidly receive instant structural data updates.
Multi-Language Support: Empoweringly enables developers to write rapid server logic in popular, typed languages like Rust, C#, and TypeScript.
ACID Compliant: Strictly maintains traditional, highly rigid relational database transaction guarantees while simultaneously acting as a blazing fast web server.

useCases.title: Multiplayer Game Backends
useCases.description: Dramatically simplifies complex backend development for highly real-time multiplayer games by seamlessly handling both volatile state and core logic in one place.

useCases.title: Real-Time Collaborative Apps
useCases.description: Efficiently powers highly interactive applications like massive document editors or dense whiteboards that absolutely require instant state synchronization across clients.

useCases.title: High-Frequency Trading Platforms
useCases.description: Heavily leverages the incredible microsecond latency to effectively build ultra-fast, massively concurrent financial and dense trading systems.

useCases.title: Serverless Edge Applications
useCases.description: Actively acts as a highly capable edge database and dense compute layer combined, massively reducing overall deployment complexity and infrastructure costs.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: SpacetimeDB is built for dedicated game developers, advanced backend engineers, and expert full-stack developers actively building incredibly real-time, stateful applications. The platform simplifies complex workflows and accelerates development timelines.
